title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, “Analysis of homozygous transgenic lines” paragraph versus Figure 3 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: “Comparative shoot-length, root-length and fresh wt. taken after 10 days-stress indicated...” for the measurements presented in Figure 3. However, the Figure 3 caption describes the same phenotypic comparison as being performed “under variable NaCl stresses kept for 7 days.” These are materially different exposure durations, especially at 200–300 mM NaCl, and the paper does not identify which duration applies to the plotted data.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, transcript analyses associated with Figure 2 and Figure 5
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly describes detecting a “37-amino acid specific PcINO1-transcript” or “37-amino acid gene transcript.” Amino acids are components of a translated protein, not of an RNA transcript. A transcript-specific PCR/qRT-PCR assay must be defined by a nucleotide sequence, primer/probe sequence, or a coding region expressed in nucleotides. As written, the assay target is biologically undefined, preventing assessment of whether the stated PcINO1-specific transcript measurements actually distinguish PcINO1 from endogenous OsINO1.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, line-selection procedure and subsequent comparison of 7PcINO1, 10PcIMT1, and 6DC1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors first expose many T3 lines to salt and select the “three best performing lines from each type,” then choose one line per construct as the “best in terms of growth parameters” (7PcINO1, 10PcIMT1, and 6DC1), and use those selected lines for later transcript, protein, metabolite, recovery, and construct-level comparisons. This is post hoc selection on the same salt-response phenotype being used as evidence of construct superiority. The comparison is also confounded by independent insertion events and their genomic positions; it cannot distinguish a PcINO1/PcIMT1/DC1 effect from exceptional-event selection or insertion-position effects. The stated three plants per condition are plants within a selected event, not independent transformation events.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and concluding Results claims concerning PcINO1 superiority and inositol as the stress-ameliorating factor
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract concludes that plants with uninterrupted inositol production “showed normal growth as in the wild-type plants without stress” and suggests that inositol itself is the stress ameliorator/switch responsible for salt tolerance. The reported evidence is observational comparison among separately transformed, preselected lines under short acute seedling stress (7–10 days) and a 12-hour molecular assay; it does not manipulate inositol independently of transgene/insertion event, establish mediation, test ion homeostasis, or measure reproductive performance/yield. Therefore it does not support assigning causality to inositol or asserting normal unstressed-equivalent growth.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract claim of salt tolerance in transgenic rice
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper presents short-term seedling survival/growth and recovery after removal of NaCl, but frames this as induction of crop salt tolerance. No evidence described here establishes durable tolerance over the rice life cycle, fertility, grain yield, or agronomic performance under saline conditions. Acute survival after selected 7–10 day assays is not sufficient to support the broader crop-tolerance conclusion.
